Well, I'll tell you what I didn't like. Nobody was acting casual, they were all pretty obviously hamming it up. I have a theatre degree so I might be more sensitive to that than some other people, but it seemed like they were laying it on pretty thick, even for youtube. The second thing I didn't like was that the conflict was a total cop-out. Having someone spontaneously commit suicide doesn't take any work on the part of the actors. It's just an external stimulus that they had to deal with. Good acting and writing follows a line; there's a beginning stasis, showing how life is normal, then there's an intrusion, something that disrupts the stasis and begins the actions of the story. What happens next should be a direct reaction to the intrusion, then the next action should be in response to that first reaction and so on. The story wasn't really consistent. On a final note, it was just really jarring for me. In college I lived with two other dudes and one of them killed himself by hanging. I don't expect you to know that, however, it's a personal thing and trigger warnings are bullshit, it just really took me out of it. I was googling for the book I used in classes to learn stronger story-writing skills, but I can't seem to be able to find the title. If I find it I'll let you know.
